prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim. Injury: neck strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1408; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following a reported low-speed head-on collision at an intersection. Insured vehicle sustained front bumper and hood damage. Insured reports no airbag deployment and drove from scene. Photos requested from insured and a recorded statement scheduled.

Entry 2: Recorded statement taken from insured. Insured states the other driver crossed the centerline while turning. Police report number obtained; officer noted minor damage and no citations issued at scene. Third-party vehicle identified and claimant's policy confirmed as active.

Entry 3: Claimant is represented by counsel. Letter of representation received today. All further contact to be routed through the attorney's office. Claimant reports neck strain and is currently under medical care. Medical records and authorization forms requested through counsel.

Entry 4: Field appraiser inspected both vehicles. Estimate prepared for insured vehicle repairs. Third-party vehicle damage consistent with reported impact speed. Liability is under review pending witness contact and the scene diagram from the responding officer.

Entry 5: Counsel's office confirmed receipt of records request and provided partial treatment notes listing cervical strain diagnosis and physical therapy referral. Reserve reviewed and adjusted for bodily injury exposure. Follow-up set for the next review cycle while medical documentation is completed.
